y_axis.note: frame edges at slip -10 and 100 percent

marker.mask_note: orange dot markers (Scarecrow); legend excluded; crop is the frame inset by 12 px

meta.source_title: Traverse Performance Characterization for the Mars Science Laboratory Rover (Heverly et al.; Journal of Field Robotics 30(6), 2013)
meta.grousers: chevron grousers at 15 deg spacing, 7.5 mm radial height (Sec 3)
meta.gravity_g: 1 (Earth test; vehicle mass chosen for Mars weight)
meta.vehicle: Scarecrow (Mars weight MSL mobility test rover, 340 kg, six wheel rocker bogie)
meta.soil: Marsyard cohesionless sand, well sorted, some subsurface moisture detected
meta.preparation: artificial sand slopes in a U shaped retaining wall, flat to 25 deg, track 5 m by 9 m
meta.comparability_note: Points are bin medians of all marker pixels found by colour masking in 1 deg slope bins (pixel weighted, so runs with more plotted samples weigh more); x_unc and y_unc combine the reading error with half the interquartile range of the masked pixels in the bin. Slip = 1 minus traverse distance over commanded distance, in percent, from 10 s windows at 1 Hz (GPS) or 2 Hz (motion capture), Eq. 2 to 4; slope is measured rover pitch. Constructed slope of well sorted sand at 1 g with some subsurface moisture (paper notes packing between grousers), so not a natural dune; vehicles embedded near 17 deg (Sec 6.3). Negative slip values are measurement noise per the paper. load_per_wheel_N derived here from Table I Earth weight 3329 N divided by 6 wheels (equal share assumed).
